propositions: Plan-review gate's decomposition criteria lack grounding in recent AI task-decomposition research and need validation against state-of-the-art practices to reduce false positives and improve flaw detection.

Post-claim ticket-description edits (3.2% of candidate tickets) signal plan-review misses; 3 of 8 reviewed tickets with edits represent genuine missed findings, all relating to asserted-capability grounding.

Gap analysis across passes 1, 2, and 4 reveals that 30% of candidate findings are dropped by later passes and 68% of tickets require ≥2 review rounds, indicating potential criterion calibration or ordering issues.

Recommendations must be falsifiable via experiment (metric + pass/fail condition) and validated against actual plan-review history to avoid introducing new false positives while improving decomposition-flaw detection.

OSS convergence on decomposition practices (15 systems, file-level patterns) and empirical data from CMU, IBM, CodePlan, and other sources provide a reproducible baseline for assessing and refining plan-review criteria.
